questions.question_html: $\int_{a-6}^{b-6}f(x+6)dx$ is equal to
questions.explanation_text: Put $t=x+6$ Then $dt=dx$ Now change the limits. When $x=a-6,$ we get $t=(a-6)+6=a$ When $x=b-6,$ we get $t=(b-6)+6=b$ So, $\int_{a-6}^{b-6}f(x+6)dx=\int_{a}^{b}f(t)dt$ The letter used for the variable does not matter in a definite integral. So, $\int_{a}^{b}f(t)dt=\int_{a}^{b}f(x)dx$ Hence, $\int_{a-6}^{b-6}f(x+6)dx=\int_{a}^{b}f(x)dx$ So the correct option is $\text{Option C}$

questions.question_html: One of the possible functions $f(x)$ which satisfies $\int_{-2}^{2}f(x)dx=0$ is
questions.explanation_text: $f(x)=log(\frac{2-x}{2+x})$ For an integral over symmetric limits $[-2,2]$ , a useful NCERT result is: If $f(x)$ is an odd function, then $\int_{-a}^{a}f(x)dx=0$ So we check whether the given function is odd. For Option A, $f(x)=log(\frac{2-x}{2+x})$ Now, $f(-x)=log(\frac{2-(-x)}{2+(-x)})$ $f(-x)=log(\frac{2+x}{2-x})$ Using the property $log(\frac{1}{A})=-logA$ we get $f(-x)=-log(\frac{2-x}{2+x})$ So, $f(-x)=-f(x)$ Hence the function is odd. Since the limits are from $-2$ to $2$ , the integral becomes zero. Thus, $\int_{-2}^{2}log(\frac{2-x}{2+x})dx=0$ So the correct answer is $\text{Option A}$
questions.explanation_html:
$f(x)=log(\frac{2-x}{2+x})$

For an integral over symmetric limits $[-2,2]$ , a useful NCERT result is:

If $f(x)$ is an odd function, then

$\int_{-a}^{a}f(x)dx=0$

So we check whether the given function is odd.

For Option A,

$f(x)=log(\frac{2-x}{2+x})$

Now,

$f(-x)=log(\frac{2-(-x)}{2+(-x)})$

$f(-x)=log(\frac{2+x}{2-x})$

Using the property

$log(\frac{1}{A})=-logA$

we get

$f(-x)=-log(\frac{2-x}{2+x})$

So,

$f(-x)=-f(x)$

Hence the function is odd. Since the limits are from $-2$ to $2$ , the integral becomes zero.

Thus,

$\int_{-2}^{2}log(\frac{2-x}{2+x})dx=0$

So the correct answer is

$\text{Option A}$

We have, $\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2}\frac{cosx}{1+e^{x}}dx$

$\begin{aligned} & =\int_{0}^{\pi/2}(\frac{cosx}{1+e^{x}}+\frac{cos(-x)}{(1+e^{-x})})dx \\ & [ \because \int_{-a}^{a}f(x)dx=\int_{0}^{a}(f(x)+f(-x))dx] \\ & =\int_{0}^{\pi/2}(\frac{cosx}{1+e^{x}}+\frac{e^{x}cosx}{1+e^{x}})dx \\ & =\int_{0}^{\pi/2}cosx(\frac{1+e^{x}}{1+e^{x}})dx \\ & =\int_{0}^{\pi/2}cosxdx=(sinx)_{0}^{\pi/2} \\ & =(sin\frac{\pi}{2}-sin0)=1 \end{aligned}$

questions.question_html: $\int_{-3}^{3}cot^{-1}xdx=$
questions.explanation_html: $\begin{aligned} & \int_{-3}^{3}cot^{-1}xdx=\int_{-3}^{3}(\frac{\pi}{2}-tan^{-1}x)dx \\ & =\int_{-3}^{3}\frac{\pi}{2}dx-\int_{-3}^{3}tan^{-1}xdx=\frac{\pi}{2}[x]_{-3}^{3}-0 \\ & ( \because \int_{-a}^{a}f(x)dx=0,\text{if}f\text{is odd functions)} \\ & =\frac{\pi}{2}[3+3]=\frac{\pi}{2} \times 6=3\pi \end{aligned}$

questions.question_html: $\int_{0}^{2}[x^{2}]dx=$
questions.explanation_html:
$\int_{0}^{2}[x^{2}]dx=\int_{0}^{1}[x^{2}]dx+\int_{1}^{\sqrt{2}}[x^{2}]dx+\int_{\sqrt{2}}^{\sqrt{3}}[x^{2}]dx+\int_{\sqrt{3}}^{2}[x^{2}]dx$

$\begin{aligned} & =\int_{0}^{1}0dx+\int_{1}^{\sqrt{2}}1dx+\int_{\sqrt{2}}^{\sqrt{3}}2dx+\int_{\sqrt{3}}^{2}3dx \\ & =[x]_{1}^{\sqrt{2}}+[2x]_{\sqrt{2}}^{\sqrt{3}}+[3x]_{\sqrt{3}}^{2} \\ & =(\sqrt{2}-1)+(2\sqrt{3}-2\sqrt{2})+(6-3\sqrt{3}) \\ & =5-\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{3} \end{aligned}$

questions.question_html: $\int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{\frac{1+x}{1-x}}dx=$
questions.explanation_html:
$\begin{aligned} & \int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{\frac{1+x}{1-x}}dx=\int_{0}^{1}\frac{1+x}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}dx \\ & =\int_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}dx+\int_{0}^{1}\frac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}dx \\ & =[sin^{-1}x]_{0}^{1}-\frac{1}{2}\int_{0}^{1}\frac{-2x}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}dx \\ & =(\frac{\pi}{2}-0)-\frac{1}{2}\int_{1}^{0}\frac{dt}{\sqrt{t}} \end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned} & \text{put}1-x^{2}=t \Rightarrow -2xdx=dt\text{at}x=0,t=1 \\ & \text{and}x=1,t=0 \\ & =\frac{\pi}{2}+\frac{1}{2}\int_{0}^{1}t^{-1/2}dt \\ & =\frac{\pi}{2}+\frac{1}{2}(\frac{t^{1/2}}{1/2})_{0}^{1}=\frac{\pi}{2}+1 \end{aligned}$

questions.question_html: $\int_{0}^{1/2}\frac{dx}{(1+x^{2})\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}$ is equal to
questions.explanation_html: $\begin{aligned} & \text{We have,}I=\int_{0}^{1/2}\frac{dx}{(1+x^{2})\sqrt{1-x^{2}}} \\ & \text{Put}x=sin\theta \Rightarrow dx=cos\theta d\theta \\ & x=0,\theta=0,x=\frac{1}{2},\theta=\frac{\pi}{6} \\ & \therefore I=\int_{0}^{\pi/6}\frac{cos\theta d\theta}{(1+sin^{2}\theta)cos\theta} \\ & \therefore I=\int_{0}^{\pi/6}\frac{d\theta}{1+sin^{2}\theta} \\ & \begin{aligned} \because & I=\frac{1}{2}\int_{0}^{1/\sqrt{3}}\frac{dt}{(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}})^{2}(+t^{2})} \\ \Rightarrow & I=\frac{1}{2}(\sqrt{2}tan^{-1}\sqrt{2}t)_{0}^{1/\sqrt{3}} \\ \Rightarrow & I=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[tan^{-1}(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}})-0] \\ \Rightarrow & I=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}tan^{-1}(\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}) \end{aligned} \end{aligned}$

questions.explanation_text: $\begin{aligned} & . \\ & \begin{aligned} & \text{Let}I=\int_{-2}^{2}|xcos\pi x|dx \\ & \begin{aligned} \Rightarrow & I=2\int_{0}^{2}|xcos\pi x|dx \end{aligned} \\ & \begin{aligned} \Rightarrow I=2[\int_{0}^{1/2}xcos\pi xdx-\int_{1/2}^{3/2}xcos\pi xdx \\ \\ +\int_{3/2}^{2}xcos\pi xdx \end{aligned} \\ & \begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow I=2[[\frac{xsin\pi x}{\pi}+\frac{cos\pi x}{\pi^{2}}]_{0}^{1/2}-[\frac{xsin\pi x}{\pi}+\frac{cos\pi x}{\pi^{2}}]_{1/2}^{3/2} \\ & \Rightarrow +[\frac{xsin\pi x}{\pi}+\frac{cos\pi x}{\pi^{2}}]_{3/2}^{2}] \\ & I=2[(\frac{1}{2\pi}+0)-(0+\frac{1}{\pi^{2}})-{(\frac{-3}{2\pi}+0)-(\frac{1}{2\pi}+0)} \\ & \Rightarrow I=2[\frac{1}{2\pi}-\frac{1}{\pi^{2}}+\frac{3}{2\pi}+\frac{1}{2\pi}+\frac{1}{\pi^{2}}+\frac{3}{2\pi}] \\ & \Rightarrow I=\frac{8}{\pi} \end{aligned} \end{aligned} \end{aligned}$

questions.explanation_text: $\begin{aligned} & \text{We have,}I=\int_{0}^{1}\frac{dx}{e^{x}+e^{-x}} \\ & \Rightarrow I=\int_{0}^{1}\frac{e^{x}}{1+e^{2x}}dx \\ & \text{put}e^{x}=t\text{and}e^{x}dx=dt\text{, where if} \\ & x=0,t=1\text{and if}x=1,t=e \\ & \therefore \\ & \Rightarrow I=\int_{1}^{e}\frac{dt}{1+t^{2}} \\ & \Rightarrow I=[tan^{-1}t]_{1}^{e} \\ & \Rightarrow I=tan^{-1}e-tan^{-1}1 \\ & \Rightarrow \\ & I=tan^{-1}e-\frac{\pi}{4} \end{aligned}$ Divide by $cos^{2}\theta$ , we get $\begin{aligned} & I=\int_{0}^{\pi/6}\frac{sec^{2}\theta d\theta}{sec^{2}\theta+tan^{2}\theta} \\ & \Rightarrow I=\int_{0}^{\pi/6}\frac{sec^{2}\theta d\theta}{1+2tan^{2}\theta} \\ & \Rightarrow I=\frac{1}{2}\int_{0}^{\pi/6}\frac{sec^{2}\theta d\theta}{(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}})^{2}+tan^{2}\theta} \\ & \text{Put}tan\theta=t,sec^{2}\theta d\theta=dt \\ & \theta=0,t=0\theta=\frac{\pi}{6},t=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \end{aligned}$
